mcqs.question: What is the correct definition of uniform circular motion?

options.A: Motion of an object in a circular path with constant speed.
options.B: Motion of an object in a straight line with constant speed.
options.C: Motion of an object in a circular path with varying speed.
options.D: Motion of an object in a straight line with varying speed.

mcqs.answer: Motion of an object in a circular path with constant speed.
mcqs.explanation: Uniform circular motion means the object travels around a circle while maintaining a constant magnitude of speed; only its direction changes, giving a continuously changing velocity. Options B, C, and D describe different types of motion.

mcqs.question: Angular position of a particle moving in a circle is measured by:

options.A: The linear distance traveled along the circumference.
options.B: The angle (in radians or degrees) subtended at the centre from a chosen reference line.
options.C: The time taken to complete one revolution.

mcqs.answer: The angle (in radians or degrees) subtended at the centre from a chosen reference line.
mcqs.explanation: Angular position is defined as the angle made by the radius vector of the particle with a fixed reference direction, usually measured in radians or degrees. Linear distance, time, and speed are unrelated to angular position.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly defines centripetal acceleration and distinguishes it from tangential acceleration?

options.A: Centripetal acceleration is directed toward the centre of the circular path with magnitude v²/r; tangential acceleration is along the direction of motion and changes the speed.
options.B: Centripetal acceleration is directed away from the centre of the circular path; tangential acceleration is perpendicular to the motion.
options.C: Centripetal acceleration is zero for uniform circular motion; tangential acceleration is v²/r.
options.D: Centripetal acceleration and tangential acceleration are the same and both point outward.

mcqs.answer: Centripetal acceleration is directed toward the centre of the circular path with magnitude v²/r; tangential acceleration is along the direction of motion and changes the speed.
mcqs.explanation: In uniform circular motion the speed is constant, so tangential acceleration is zero. The required acceleration is centripetal, always pointing radially inward with magnitude v²/r. Options B, C, and D contain incorrect directions or magnitudes.

mcqs.question: A particle moves in a circle of radius r with angular speed ω (rad/s). What is its linear speed v?
mcqs.explanation: Linear speed v is related to angular speed ω by v = ωr, because the arc length traveled in time t is s = rθ and θ = ωt, giving v = ds/dt = rω. The other formulas are dimensionally incorrect.

mcqs.question: A car travels around a circular track of radius 50 m with a constant speed of 20 m/s. What is the magnitude of its centripetal acceleration?
mcqs.explanation: Centripetal acceleration a_c = v²/r = (20 m/s)² / 50 m = 400 / 50 = 8 m/s². Option B matches this value; the other options are results of incorrect arithmetic.

mcqs.question: Which of the following situations best exemplifies uniform circular motion?

options.A: A car moving at a constant speed around a circular race track.
options.B: A car accelerating while turning around a circular curve.
options.C: A satellite following an elliptical orbit around Earth.
options.D: A particle oscillating back and forth along a straight line.

mcqs.answer: A car moving at a constant speed around a circular race track.
mcqs.explanation: Uniform circular motion requires a constant speed along a circular path, which is exactly described in option A. Option B involves speed change, option C is not circular (elliptical), and option D is linear motion.

mcqs.question: Which statement about angular position is **incorrect**?

options.A: It is measured from a fixed reference line.
options.B: It can be expressed in radians or degrees.
options.C: It remains constant for a particle moving with constant speed in a circle.
options.D: It increases as the particle moves around the circle.

mcqs.answer: It remains constant for a particle moving with constant speed in a circle.
mcqs.explanation: Even when speed is constant, the particle’s direction changes, so its angular position continuously changes. Options A, B, and D correctly describe angular position; option C is the misconception.

mcqs.question: Why does a particle moving in a circle at constant speed experience a centripetal acceleration directed toward the centre?

options.B: Because the direction of its velocity vector is continuously changing.
options.C: Because a net outward (centrifugal) force acts on it.
options.D: Because friction is the only force acting.

mcqs.answer: Because the direction of its velocity vector is continuously changing.
mcqs.explanation: Centripetal acceleration arises from the continual change in the direction of velocity, even when the speed is constant. This change requires a net inward force, giving acceleration toward the centre. Option A is wrong (speed is constant), C misstates direction, and D is irrelevant to the general case.
